purpose: Preview-only study of a proposed playful toy-world art direction. This is character and material concept art, not a gameplay screenshot or an approved implementation comp.
approval: User: Yeah I like this this looks a lot better. Approved September 29, 2026.
approvalScope: Visual direction, character silhouettes, saturated toy materials and terrain. This study is not a pixel layout contract: its scene is illustrative and the existing real mission geometry and native controls remain functional.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: preview-only art direction study for an existing original isometric construction game, titled Untitled. This is concept art for a review, not a screenshot or a promotional poster.
Primary request: Show a clear playful toy-world direction that makes three existing game units feel distinct and alive. The game involves moving specialist units around square terrain tiles, carrying physical parts and batteries, and rebuilding from pieces. Its reference is the straightforward, boldly colored pre-rendered toy graphics of early-2000s browser games. Give it its own original shapes and material vocabulary.
Composition: One polished wide landscape art-study sheet, about 3:2. The left two-thirds shows an isometric playable-looking patch of terrain at a fixed orthographic camera angle: two small green land areas divided by clear bright cyan water, a short plank bridge, square grid cells, chunky trees and rocks, two colorful rovers, one six-legged enemy, loose construction parts and a goal flag. Readable open ground between objects, no clutter. The right third is a neat vertical column of three enlarged character studies with the exact small labels "Scout", "Hauler", and "Bristleback". Keep the character studies fully inside the frame. The scene and studies use precisely the same art language and models.
Characters:
Scout: a small eager bright lime-green four-wheeled exploration toy with a short rounded hood, two simple inquisitive headlight-like eyes on the front, a springy antenna, big charcoal rubber wheels, and a clearly separate bright blue battery cartridge at the rear. It looks speedy and curious. Use only a few large strong forms; front eyes should read at small game size.
Hauler: a much broader and lower tangerine-orange four-wheeled utility toy, a deep open cargo bed visibly holding a few colorful modular parts, large dark rubber tires, contrasting turquoise axle/joints, a wide blunt nose with calm expressive headlight eyes. It looks sturdy and slightly lumbering. Its silhouette must be unmistakably different from Scout.
Bristleback: an original mischievous wild mechanical critter with six short articulated legs, a cherry-red segmented shell, three large ivory ridges/spines, small sharp black eyes, and a snout. It is slightly funny but clearly a hazard. Its body uses visible fitted parts like the rovers, with a completely different animal silhouette.
Materials: simple glossy molded toy plastic, solid saturated color panels, visible wedge-shaped panels, chunky hinges, sockets, wheels and battery cartridges, broad highlights and firm shading. Strong dark contours where necessary. The modular construction should be legible without intricate sci-fi details.
World: spring-green grass tiles with thick raised earthy sides, bright cyan shallow water tiles with a few crisp ripples, sunny yellow sand, plastic-like trees with big rounded leaves and dark trunks, simple chunky stones. A deep ink-blue field behind the scene. Loose parts are bright yellow, blue, red chunky curved plates and connectors, recognizable next to a cylindrical blue battery. The flag is small and yellow.
Style: crisp clean isometric sprite-inspired digital illustration with the clarity of deliberately simple pre-rendered toy game assets. Confident saturated color, clear silhouette, solid light and shade. Slight amusing asymmetry. All units fit on individual grid cells in the scene and are readable as clickable objects. Cheerful mechanical personality, practical game readability.
Avoid: LEGO logos, LEGO brick shapes, studs or minifigures, copied vehicles or creatures from any existing game, beige/pastel cozy-game palette, muted sage and gray teal, painterly landscapes, photographic realism, futuristic weapons, tiny greebles, lush environmental clutter, enormous cute character heads, mobile-game menu chrome, fake HUD or gameplay text, marketing copy. Only the three character labels, plus an unobtrusive small "Untitled — art study" label at the top.
